analysis.subject: history
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers transaction terms for territory west of Mississippi, negotiation scope and price, Jefferson constitutional concerns, sequence of expansions to contiguous borders, sectional tensions over slavery with compromises, and impact on Native peoples

overview.headline: Territory purchase doubled nation size and deepened sectional conflict

keyPoints.point: The purchase doubled the size of the nation while expanding westward
keyPoints.quote: For roughly 4 cents an acre, the United States doubled its size, expanding the nation westward.

keyPoints.point: Negotiators Livingston and Monroe were authorized to pay for the port of New Orleans and the Floridas
keyPoints.quote: negotiators Robert Livingston and James Monroe were authorized to pay France up to $10 million

keyPoints.point: Jefferson was a strict interpreter who wondered if Government was authorized to acquire new territory
keyPoints.quote: President Thomas Jefferson was generally a strict interpreter of the Constitution who wondered if the U.S. Government

keyPoints.point: Expansion exposed sectional weaknesses between North and South related to slavery
keyPoints.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery

keyPoints.point: Purchase ignored impact on Native people who were forcibly moved to reservations and lost tribal lands
keyPoints.quote: Ultimately, Native people were forcibly moved on to reservations, losing vast acreage of their tribal lands

keyTerms.gloss: formal transfer of land by treaty from one holder to another
keyTerms.quote: The Louisiana Purchase was the first major cession of land in a long series of expansions that span the 19th century.

keyTerms.gloss: divisions between North and South over slavery that threatened national unity
keyTerms.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery

keyTerms.gloss: fragile compromise agreement meant to keep balance between free states and slave states
keyTerms.quote: required a series of fragile compromises (notably the Missouri Compromise and the Compromise of 1850)

keyTerms.gloss: tribal lands where Native people were forcibly moved and confined
keyTerms.quote: Ultimately, Native people were forcibly moved on to reservations, losing vast acreage of their tribal lands

keyTerms.gloss: leader who reads the Constitution narrowly and questions Government authority to act
keyTerms.quote: President Thomas Jefferson was generally a strict interpreter of the Constitution who wondered if the U.S. Government
